source.title: Some open problems on excluding a uniform matroid

accepted.question_text: For positive integers a and b, can one find a qualitative structure theorem for the class of matroids with no uniform matroid U_{a,b} as a minor? The desired theorem should be analogous in spirit to the Graph Minors Structure Theorem: every matroid excluding U_{a,b} should be constructible in a tree-like way from basic classes such as Dowling matroids, their duals, and matroids representable over finite fields over which U_{a,b} is not representable, without generating classes containing arbitrary uniform matroids as minors.
accepted.context_brief: Structure theorem excluding a uniform minor

evidence.quote: Problem 1.1. Let a and b be positive integers. Find a qualitative structure theorem for the class of matroids with no Ua,b-minor.
The hope is to find a constructive structural description for all matroids with no Ua,b-minor

accepted.question_text: For every finite field F, is the class of F-representable matroids well-quasi-ordered by the minor relation? Equivalently, must every infinite set of F-representable matroids contain two members such that one is isomorphic to a minor of the other?
accepted.context_brief: Well-quasi-ordering over finite fields

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.1 (Well-Quasi-Ordering Conjecture). For any finite field F, any infinite set of F-representable matroids contains two matroids, one isomorphic to a minor of the other.

accepted.question_text: For every finite field F and every fixed F-representable matroid N, is there a polynomial-time algorithm that, given an F-represented matroid as input, decides whether the input matroid has N as a minor?
accepted.context_brief: Minor testing over finite fields

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.2 (Minor-Testing Conjecture). For any finite field F and F-representable matroid N, there is a polynomial-time algorithm that tests for an N-minor in any F-represented matroid.

accepted.question_text: For every finite field F, are there only finitely many excluded minors, up to isomorphism, for the class of F-representable matroids?
accepted.context_brief: Rota finite-field excluded-minor conjecture

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.3 (Rota’s Conjecture, 1971). For any finite field F, there are, up to isomorphism, only finitely many excluded minors for the class of F-representable matroids.

accepted.question_text: For every finite field F, is there a polynomial-time algorithm that takes two matrices A1 and A2 over F with the same column-index set and decides whether the matroids represented by the two matrices are equal, that is, whether M(A1) = M(A2)?
accepted.context_brief: Matrix representation equivalence over finite fields

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.4 (Equivalence-Testing Conjecture). For any finite field F, there is a polynomial-time algorithm that, given two matrices A1 and A2 over F with the same set of column indices, tests whether M(A1) = M(A2).

accepted.question_text: Is there a uniform integer n such that every excluded minor for the class of real-representable matroids has branch-width at most n?
accepted.context_brief: Branch-width of excluded minors for real representability

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1. Is there an integer n such that all excluded minors for the class of R-representable matroids have branch-width ≤ n?

accepted.question_text: Is there an integer k such that no excluded minor for the class of real-representable matroids contains the uniform matroid U_{k,2k} as a minor?
accepted.context_brief: Uniform minors in excluded minors for real representability

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2. Is there an integer k such that no excluded minor for the class of R-representable matroids contains a Uk,2k-minor?

accepted.question_text: For every integer k, does there exist an integer n such that every excluded minor M for the class of real-representable matroids that has no U_{k,2k}-minor must have branch-width at most n?
accepted.context_brief: Bounded branch-width when large uniform minors are excluded

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.3. For every integer k there is an integer n such that, if M is an excluded minor for the class of R-representable matroids and M has no Uk,2k-minor, then M has branch-width at most n.

accepted.question_text: For every real-representable matroid N, does there exist an excluded minor M for the class of real-representable matroids such that M contains N as a minor?
accepted.context_brief: Universality of real-representability excluded minors

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.4. For any R-representable matroid N, there is an excluded minor M for the class of R-representable matroids such that M contains an N-minor.

accepted.question_text: Can non-real-representability of a matroid given by a rank oracle be certified using only a polynomial number of rank evaluations?
accepted.context_brief: Polynomial certificates for non-real-representability

evidence.quote: Problem 4.5. Can non-R-representability be certified using only a polynomial number of rank-evaluations?

accepted.question_text: For every fixed positive integer k, can non-real-representability of matroids of branch-width k be certified using only a polynomial number of rank evaluations?
accepted.context_brief: Certificates for bounded-branch-width matroids

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.6. Let k be a fixed positive integer. For matroids of branch-width k, non-R-representability can be certified using only a polynomial number of rank-evaluations.

accepted.question_text: For any finite field F and any two matroids, are there only finitely many F-representable intertwines of the two matroids, up to isomorphism? Here a matroid M is an intertwine of matroids N1 and N2 when M contains both an N1-minor and an N2-minor, but no proper minor of M contains both.
accepted.context_brief: Finite representable intertwines over finite fields

evidence.quote: A matroid M is an intertwine of two matroids N1 and N2 if M contains an N1- and an N2-minor but no proper minor of M does.
Conjecture 5.1. For any finite field F, there are, up to isomorphism, only finitely many F-representable intertwines for any two matroids.

accepted.question_text: For every pair of matroids N1 and N2 and every positive integer k, does there exist an integer n such that every intertwine M of N1 and N2 with no U_{k,2k}-minor has branch-width at most n?
accepted.context_brief: Branch-width of intertwines avoiding uniform minors

evidence.quote: A matroid M is an intertwine of two matroids N1 and N2 if M contains an N1- and an N2-minor but no proper minor of M does.

Conjecture 5.3. For every pair of matroids N1 and N2 and every positive integer k there is an integer n such that, if M is an intertwine of N1 and N2 and M does not contain a Uk,2k-minor, then M has branch-width at most n.

accepted.question_text: For any positive integers a and b and any matroid M, are there only finitely many intertwines, up to isomorphism, of M and the uniform matroid U_{a,b}?
accepted.context_brief: Finiteness of intertwines with a uniform matroid

evidence.quote: A matroid M is an intertwine of two matroids N1 and N2 if M contains an N1- and an N2-minor but no proper minor of M does.
Problem 5.4. For any positive integers a and b and any matroid M, are there, up to isomorphism, only finitely many intertwines of M and Ua,b?

accepted.question_text: For every integer k, does there exist an integer n such that every matroid M of sufficiently large branch-width, namely branch-width at least n, has either M or its dual M* containing one of the following minors: U_{k,2k}, the cycle matroid of a k by k grid, or the bicircular matroid of the k by k grid? The bicircular matroid B(G) of a graph G is obtained from the framed Dowling matroid B+(G) by deleting the vertex basis V, after placing each edge freely on the line spanned by its endpoints and each loop in parallel with its incident vertex.
accepted.context_brief: Large branch-width forces basic minors

evidence.quote: The bicircular matroid of G, denoted B(G), is defined as B+(G) \ V.

Conjecture 6.1. For any integer k there is an integer n such that if M has branch-width ≥ n, then either M or M∗ contains one of the following minors: Uk,2k, the cycle matroid of a k × k grid, or the bicircular matroid of the k × k grid.

accepted.question_text: What are the excluded minors for the class of Dowling matroids? In this setting, a matroid M with a basis V is a framed Dowling matroid when every fundamental circuit with respect to V has size at most 3, and M \ V is called a Dowling matroid.
accepted.context_brief: Excluded minors for Dowling matroids

evidence.quote: If each of the fundamental circuits of M, with respect to the basis V, have size at most 3, then we call M a framed Dowling matroid with joint set V and we call the matroid M \ V a Dowling matroid.
Find the excluded minors for the class of Dowling matroids.

accepted.question_text: Can Dowling matroids be recognized in polynomial time, where a Dowling matroid is a matroid M \ V obtained from a framed Dowling matroid M with basis V whose fundamental circuits with respect to V all have size at most 3?
accepted.context_brief: Polynomial-time recognition of Dowling matroids

evidence.quote: If each of the fundamental circuits of M, with respect to the basis V, have size at most 3, then we call M a framed Dowling matroid with joint set V and we call the matroid M \ V a Dowling matroid.
Can we recognize Dowling matroids in polynomial time?

accepted.question_text: What are the excluded minors for the class of Dowling matroids over the real field R? A matroid is a Dowling matroid over a field F when it can be extended to an F-representable framed Dowling matroid, equivalently when it has a representation over F with at most two nonzero entries in each column.
accepted.context_brief: Excluded minors for real Dowling matroids

evidence.quote: For a field F, we will call a matroid a Dowling matroid over F if it can be extended to an F-representable framed Dowling matroid or, equivalently, it admits a representation over F with at most two non-zero entries in each column.
Find the excluded minors for the class of Dowling matroids over R.

accepted.question_text: Can Dowling matroids over the real field R be recognized in polynomial time? Here a matroid is a Dowling matroid over R if it can be extended to an R-representable framed Dowling matroid, equivalently if it has a real representation with at most two nonzero entries in each column.
accepted.context_brief: Polynomial-time recognition of real Dowling matroids

evidence.quote: For a field F, we will call a matroid a Dowling matroid over F if it can be extended to an F-representable framed Dowling matroid or, equivalently, it admits a representation over F with at most two non-zero entries in each column.
Can we recognize Dowling matroids over R in polynomial time.

accepted.question_text: For which fields is the uniform matroid U_{a,b} representable?
accepted.context_brief: Field representability of uniform matroids

evidence.quote: Problem 6.3. Over which fields is Ua,b representable?

accepted.question_text: For Lemma 7.2, how large must n be as a function of k so that every elementary projection M of the uniform matroid U_{n,2n} has a U_{k,2k}-minor? An elementary projection of N1 is a matroid N2 for which there is a matroid M and an element e with N1 = M \ e and N2 = M/e.
accepted.context_brief: Quantitative bound in elementary projection lemma

evidence.quote: If there is a matroid M and an element e ∈ E(M) such that N1 = M \ e and N2 = M/e, then we say that N2 is an elementary projection of N1
Lemma 7.2. For any positive integer k there is an integer n such that if M is an elementary projection of Un,2n, then M has a Uk,2k-minor.
It would be nice to know how large n needs to be as a function of k.

accepted.question_text: For a fixed integer t > 1, can one efficiently compute tau_t(M), the minimum number of rank-t flats needed to cover all elements of a matroid M?
accepted.context_brief: Efficient computation of flat-cover number tau_t

evidence.quote: For a matroid M and integer t we let τt(M) denote the minimum number of rank-t flats that are required to cover all elements of M. Thus τ1(M) is the number of points (rank-one flats) in M. (For fixed t > 1, can we compute τt(M) efficiently?)

accepted.question_text: Let C be a minor-closed class of matroids that does not contain all uniform matroids, and let t be the least integer such that C does not contain all uniform matroids of rank t+1. Must C satisfy one of the following three growth alternatives for simple matroids M in C: tau_t(M) is bounded linearly in the rank r(M); C contains all graphic matroids or all bicircular matroids and tau_t(M) is bounded quadratically in r(M); or C contains all GF(q)-representable matroids for some prime power q and tau_t(M) is bounded by a constant times q^{r(M)}?
accepted.context_brief: Growth-rate trichotomy using tau_t

evidence.quote: For a matroid M and integer t we let τt(M) denote the minimum number of rank-t flats that are required to cover all elements of M.
Conjecture 8.2. Let M be a minor-closed class of matroids that does not contain all uniform matroids and let t be minimum such that M does not contain all uniform matroids of rank t + 1. Then either
there exists c ∈ R such that τt(M) ≤ cr(M) for all simple matroids M ∈ M
M contains either all graphic matroids or all bicircular matroids and there exists c ∈ R such that τt(M) ≤ cr(M)2 for all simple matroids M ∈M
there is a prime-power q and c ∈ R such that M contains all GF(q)-representable matroids and τt(M) ≤ cqr(M) for all simple matroids M ∈M.

accepted.question_text: For finite fields F1 and F2 of different characteristic and every positive integer k, does there exist an integer n such that any matroid M with two n-interconnected minors PG(n,F1) and PG(n,F2) must contain a U_{k,2k}-minor? Two minors N1 and N2 are k-interconnected in M when every separation (X,Y) of N1 from N2 satisfies r_M(X)+r_M(Y)-r(M) at least k.
accepted.context_brief: Incompatible projective-geometry minors over different characteristics

evidence.quote: We say that N1 and N2 are k-interconnected in M if for each pair (X, Y ) separating N1 from N2, we have rM (X) + rM (Y ) − r(M) ≥ k.

Conjecture 9.1. Let F1 and F2 be finite fields of different characteristic and let k be a positive integer. Then there is an integer n such that, if M is a matroid with two n-interconnected minors PG(n,F1) and PG(n,F2), then M contains a Uk,2k-minor.

accepted.question_text: For every positive integer k, does there exist an integer n such that any matroid M with two n-interconnected minors B(G_n^+) and B(G_n^+)^* must contain a U_{k,2k}-minor? Here G_n^+ is the graph obtained by adding an apex vertex to an n by n grid, and B(G) denotes the bicircular matroid of a graph G.
accepted.context_brief: Incompatible bicircular grid minors and duals

evidence.quote: The bicircular matroid of G, denoted B(G), is defined as B+(G) \ V.
The graph G+ n is constructed by adding an apex vertex to an n × n grid.
Conjecture 9.2. For any positive integer k, there is an integer n such that, if M is a matroid with two n-interconnected minors B(G+ n ) and B(G+n )∗, then M contains a Uk,2k-minor.

accepted.question_text: For every positive integer k, does there exist an integer n such that any matroid M with two n-interconnected minors B(G_n^+) and M(G_n^+)^* must contain a U_{k,2k}-minor? Here G_n^+ is the graph obtained by adding an apex vertex to an n by n grid, B(G) is the bicircular matroid of G, and M(G) is the cycle matroid of G.
accepted.context_brief: Incompatible bicircular and dual cycle grid minors

evidence.quote: The bicircular matroid of G, denoted B(G), is defined as B+(G) \ V.
The graph G+ n is constructed by adding an apex vertex to an n × n grid.
Conjecture 9.3. For any positive integer k, there is an integer n such that, if M is a matroid with two n-interconnected minors B(G+ n ) and M(G+n )∗, then M contains a Uk,2k-minor.

accepted.question_text: For every positive integer k, does there exist an integer n such that any matroid M with two n-interconnected minors M(G_n^+) and M(G_n^+)^* either contains a U_{k,2k}-minor or contains a minor isomorphic to a rank-k projective geometry over some finite field? Here G_n^+ is obtained by adding an apex vertex to an n by n grid, and M(G) denotes the cycle matroid of G.
accepted.context_brief: Incompatible cycle grid minors and duals

evidence.quote: The graph G+ n is constructed by adding an apex vertex to an n × n grid.

Conjecture 9.4. For any positive integer k, there is an integer n such that, if M is a matroid with two n-interconnected minors M(G+ n ) and M(G+n )∗, then either M contains a Uk,2k-minor or M contains a minor isomorphic to a rank-k projective geometry over some finite field.

accepted.question_text: For every positive integer k, does there exist an integer n such that any binary matroid M with two n-interconnected minors M(K_n) and M(K_n)^* must contain a PG(k,2)-minor?
accepted.context_brief: Robertson-Seymour binary clique-dual conjecture

evidence.quote: Conjecture 9.5. For any positive integer k there is an integer n such that, if M is a binary matroid with two n-interconnected minors M(Kn) and M(Kn)∗, then M contains a PG(k, 2)-minor.

accepted.question_text: For every positive integer k, does there exist an integer n such that any binary matroid M with an M(K_n)-minor and an M(K_n)^*-minor has a minor isomorphic to the direct sum M(K_k) ⊕ M(K_k)^*?
accepted.context_brief: Disjoint clique and dual-clique minors in binary matroids

evidence.quote: Conjecture 9.6. For any positive integer k, there is an integer n such that, if M is a binary matroid with an M(Kn)-minor and an M(Kn)∗-minor, then M has an M(Kk) ⊕ M(Kk)∗-minor.

accepted.question_text: For positive integers a and b, can one find a qualitative structure theorem for the class of round matroids with no U_{a,b}-minor? A matroid is round when it does not contain two disjoint cocircuits.
accepted.context_brief: Structure theorem for round matroids excluding a uniform minor

evidence.quote: Recall that a matroid is round if it does not contain two disjoint cocircuits.
Problem 10.1. Let a and b be positive integers. Find a qualitative structure theorem for the class of round matroids with no Ua,b-minor.

accepted.question_text: For every positive integer k, does there exist an integer n such that every round matroid with a B(G_n^+)^*-minor contains a U_{k,2k}-minor? Here round means having no two disjoint cocircuits, G_n^+ is obtained from an n by n grid by adding an apex vertex, and B(G) is the bicircular matroid of G.
accepted.context_brief: Round matroids with dual bicircular grid minors

evidence.quote: Recall that a matroid is round if it does not contain two disjoint cocircuits.
The graph G+ n is constructed by adding an apex vertex to an n × n grid.
Conjecture 10.2. For any positive integer k, there is an integer n such that, if M is a round matroid with a B(G+ n )∗-minor, then M contains a Uk,2k-minor.

accepted.question_text: For every positive integer k, does there exist an integer n such that every round real-representable matroid with an M(G_n^+)^*-minor contains a U_{k,2k}-minor? Here G_n^+ is obtained by adding an apex vertex to an n by n grid, and M(G) denotes the cycle matroid of G.
accepted.context_brief: Round real-representable matroids with dual grid-cycle minors

evidence.quote: The graph G+ n is constructed by adding an apex vertex to an n × n grid.
Conjecture 10.3. For any positive integer k, there is an integer n such that, if M is a round R-representable matroid with an M(G+ n )∗-minor, then M contains a Uk,2k-minor.

accepted.question_text: Can one find a structural characterization of the class of round real-representable matroids with no U_{3,6}-minor?
accepted.context_brief: Round real-representable matroids without U_{3,6}

evidence.quote: Problem 10.4. Find a structural characterization for the class of round R-representable matroids with no U3,6-minor.

accepted.question_text: Is every infinite sequence of real-representable matroids with no U_{3,6}-minor well-quasi-ordered by the minor relation? Equivalently, must there be indices j > i at least 1 such that M_j contains a minor isomorphic to M_i?
accepted.context_brief: Well-quasi-ordering without U_{3,6}

evidence.quote: Conjecture 10.5. If (M1, M2,...) is an infinite sequence of R-representable matroids with no U3,6-minor, then there exist integers j > i ≥ 1 such that Mj contains a minor isomorphic to Mi.

accepted.question_text: Let F be a field over which U_{a,b} is not representable. Can one give a qualitative structure theorem for matroids with no U_{a,b}-minor that have a spanning PG(k,F)-restriction?

accepted.context_brief: Structure with a spanning bicircular-clique restriction

Give a qualitative structure theorem for the matroids with no Ua,b-minor that have a spanning B(Kn)-restriction.
